leads.name: The Kasteellinden of Nijenrode

location.address: Kasteel Nijenrode, Straatweg 25, Breukelen (viewed from the public road/riverbank, not the private castle courtyard)

leads.access: Free to VIEW, but not to approach. The two lindens stand on the castle square of Kasteel Nijenrode, a moated island that is the private grounds of Nyenrode Business University and not freely open; however, two independent sources confirm the trees are genuinely visible from the public road (Straatweg, which runs beside the moat) and from the river Vecht, which is public waterway. This is a view-only tree per the Hobart exception (CLAUDE.md 2026-08-13): the pin marks the public viewing point along the road/riverbank, not the private courtyard itself. The castle interior and park can only be entered on an organised tour (e.g. via the Vechtstreekmuseum or Open Monumentendag).
leads.transport: Straatweg, Breukelen, on the river Vecht; roughly 10-15 minutes' walk from Breukelen NS railway station (not independently verified this pass).
leads.verify_notes: Bomenbieb.nl lead ('kasteellinden nijenrode', planted band 1650-1750, species_nl hollandse-linde) gave the coordinate for the trees themselves (on the private courtyard); the pin here is deliberately loosened to 'approximate' because per the view-only rule the honest pin is the public viewing point, not the exact private-ground location of the trunks. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES both state the same access fact in nearly identical words: the trees are 'visible from the park, from within the castle, from the public road and from the river Vecht' (varnws.nl, reporting the 2022 National Trees Top 50 nomination, and a second source drawing on the same rijksmonumenten/monumenten.nl heritage listing). AGE: varnws.nl (2022 article) says the lindens 'have defined the castle's appearance for 270 years', implying a planting date around 1752, which sits at the later end of bomenbieb's own 1650-1750 band; used a range spanning both (250 to 376 years as of 2026) rather than forcing a single number. Note there may be more than one notable pair of lindens on the Nijenrode grounds (a separate mention of 'two distinctive lindens on the island, west of the balcony, dating from 1780' turned up in one search summary but was not confirmed on a fetched page this pass and may describe the same pair or a different one; a future pass should resolve this before writing the story). GIRTH/HEIGHT: not found this pass; left empty rather than guessed. HISTORY: the trees were nominated for the Nationale Bomen Top 50 in 2022 (public voting ran 1 June to 1 July 2022) specifically because they are described as 'visually defining' for the whole Vechtstreek stretch of river, and because maintaining trees this prominent and this old takes real, continuous care. Kasteel Nijenrode itself is a moated late-medieval castle, rebuilt over centuries, now home to Nyenrode Business University; its walled castle square carries an 18th-century marble rooster on a stone base. SINGLE-TREE-DESTINATION CANDIDATE: no Ancient Trees page exists for Breukelen. This is arguably an ensemble (a symmetrical pair) rather than one tree, but it passes the compact-and-famous ensemble test (CLAUDE.md, the Lomanstraat/Meiji Jingu standard): one obvious place to stand (the road/riverbank opposite the castle), famous specifically as this pair, and nationally nominated as such. Awaiting a place/page decision; not published by this pass.
